title: Proportional-Integral microbatch stabilizer with GPU headroom awareness
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Under sustained high QPS we observe oscillatory microbatch thresholds that cause short-term GPU memory pressure, KV cache churn, and P95 latency violations. This ticket implements a controller that continuously adjusts microbatch admission thresholds using a Proportional-Integral (PI) control law combined with a GPU headroom estimator and KV-cache health signals. Goals: stabilize microbatch sizes during spikes, keep P95 latency within SLO, avoid OOMs and excessive KV eviction while preserving throughput efficiency.
acceptance_criteria: PI controller implemented in admission service with configuration feature flag
Controller uses three inputs: queue length derivative, measured P95 latency, and GPU free memory estimate
Observed reduction in microbatch oscillation amplitude by >= 40% under synthetic spike test compared to baseline
No regressions in median latency or throughput; P95 latency stays within configured SLO for 95% of runs
KV cache eviction rate under spike load reduced or bounded (no thrashing) compared to baseline
Safe fallbacks: if GPU headroom estimator reports < 10% free, controller immediately forces conservative floor microbatch and signals alert
technical_notes: Control law: delta_threshold = Kp * error + Ki * integral(error) where error = target_p95_ms - measured_p95_ms; thresholds bounded by [min_batch, max_batch] and step-limited to avoid large jumps
GPU headroom estimator: combines free VRAM from driver metrics, per-GPU active allocation histogram, and KV-cache retention ratio to compute a conservative headroom percentage
Admission pipeline integration: controller exposes continuous target_batch_size that the admission layer uses as soft goal; microbatcher still respects request affinity and latency overrides
KV-cache signals: hit_rate, eviction_rate, and compact_cycles are weighted into control loop to bias controller toward smaller batches if cache shows thrashing
Safety: incorporate a cooldown timer and additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease (AIMD) fallback for pathological traffic patterns
Telemetry: emit controller state (Kp/Ki effective contribution, integral value, headroom_pct, chosen_batch_target) at 1s granularity to runtime-dash for correlation
design_decisions: Choose PI over PID to avoid derivative sensitivity to noisy P95 samples; use derivative-like smoothing via exponential moving average on input signals
Soft target approach: controller recommends batch target rather than forcibly changing kernel-level batch aggregation to allow microbatcher to preserve affinity and continuity
Prefer conservative headroom estimate to minimize OOM risk; err on side of smaller batches when headroom < 15%
Expose three knobs to ops: target_p95_ms, min_batch, max_batch; keep Kp/Ki tunable via remote config for rapid iteration
rollout_plan: Feature behind opt-in feature flag; 1% traffic canary for 48h in canary region
If canary meets acceptance criteria, ramp to 10% for 24h with active monitoring of P95, OOMs, and KV evaporation metrics
Progressively roll to 50% then 100% over one week, with automatic rollback trigger if OOMs > threshold or P95 regresses > 20%
Provide ops dashboard card with controller state and emergency switch to toggle to legacy admission
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller math, bound checks, and config parsing
Integration test in staging: synthetic spike generator (Poisson bursts + steady base QPS) comparing baseline vs PI controller behavior
Chaos test: simulate sudden GPU memory reclamation delay and ensure controller does not oscillate into unsafe region
Benchmark: end-to-end throughput and cost-per-token at 1%, 10%, and 100% traffic to quantify efficiency impact
Load test with varied KV workload patterns (read-heavy, write-heavy, TTL churn) to verify cache stability improvements

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Noisy P95 input causes controller instability -> Mitigation: EMA smoothing of P95 and clamping of integral term
Risk: Headroom estimator mismatches real allocation -> Mitigation: conservative bias + safety floor to min_batch and rapid alerting
Risk: Interaction with autoscaler and dedicated capacity -> Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler team, add priority signal to avoid race conditions
Risk: KV cache sudden eviction due to compaction -> Mitigation: feed compact_cycles into controller and temporarily reduce batch target when compaction detected
